recipes.name: Seven-Up Pound Cake
ingredients_raw: 7 fluid ounces lemon-lime flavored carbonated beverage

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C). Grease and flour a 10-inch Bundt pan.

In a large bowl, cream together butter, shortening, and sugar until light and fluffy. Beat in eggs, one at a time, then stir in vanilla and lemon extract. Beat in flour alternately with lemon-lime soda, mixing just until incorporated. Pour batter into the prepared pan.
Bake in the preheated oven until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean, about 70 minutes. Allow to cool on a cake rack for 30 minutes before removing from the pan.

raw_recipe.headline: Seven-Up Pound Cake
raw_recipe.description: This Seven-Up pound cake is an old-fashioned favorite. Dense and buttery, it's flavored with a can of carbonated lemon-lime soda for added rise.

review.reviewBody: My family came for a family reunion and I ended up making this cake 7 times during a 4 day period. It was easy and everyone loved it. It had a good texture. I jazzed up the flavor by adding a seven up and powered sugar glaze.

It was an easy recipe to follow. I used butter flavored Crisco for the shorting part. I also used the zest of a large lemon (because I doubled the recipe to make 2 cakes) otherwise I would have used a "regular" size lemon. I don't like the taste of lemon extract so I prefer to use fresh lemon juice and reduce the amount of 7up by the same amount. ie if I get 1/4 cup of lemon juice out of my lemon, I will reduce the 7up by 1/4 cup.

This is the kind of recipe that makes you happy to bake! I used it as a base for a Boston Cream Pie, so omitted the lemon extract and doubled the vanilla. Followed the recipe otherwise, baked it exactly 70 minutes, cooled it for 1 hour before removing it from the bundt pan. Use a heavy bundt pan; it's much easier to get good results if your pan doesn't wobble around when you handle it. I put it back in the pan once it cooled completely and covered it with saran overnight. The next day I split it, filled it with Creme Patissiere lightened with a little whipped cream, and topped it with a simple dark chocolate ganache. Perfection!

I made this cake 2 days ago, and it is already gone! My Fiance' and mother in law destroyed it before it even got a chance to cool! The only thing that I did differently was add 3 cups of sugar and 5 eggs. Its not listed on here, but I made a glaze to go along with it. To make the glaze, you need 1/4 cup of 7 up and a 1/2 cup sugar. Cook in a saucepan until the sugar is dissolved. While the cake is still warm, take a toothpick and punch holes through out the cake and pour the glaze over the cake. The glaze really made the cake yummy! I plan on making this cake again in the near future!

Made this cake today 9/4/2013 and half of the cake is already gone. My son said I should have made two. I followed the directions exactly. Once cake was out of the oven I poked holes on the top and pour a glaze I made with powder sugar, 7up, lemon extract and vanilla extract. I will be making this again and again!!!

Everyone loved this cake. Only changes were that I used cake flour and cream soda. I did not beat the cream and sugar for 20 minutes - only until light in color and fluffy - maybe 5 - 7 minutes. Made for a campfire gathering and the cake was gobbled up. I served with a variety of fresh fruit sauces and whipped cream I made to top it off.

This is such a great recipe! So tasty so moist! This recipe makes for great cupcakes too as I didn't have a bundt cake pan. I used 2 Tbs of orange zest in lieu of lemon extract because I didn't have that either. Turned out great! I sent it with my husband to share with coworkers at work, he said it was gone within minutes. Loved it!

I made this cake for the first time for Thanksgiving, it was a hit. I really liked the ease of the directions. I followed the steps but I did however take the advice of some f the prior reviews and added more more vanilla and lemon. I also used butter flavored shortening. My bunt pans where very short, so I divided it into 2 pans. This will be in my repertoire for many more years to come. Making two today for Christmas as gifts.

My family loved the cake after I tweeked it a little. I added 3/4c 7up, zest of two limes and the juice of both also. Then I put a glaze on it using icing sugar, soda and juice of 1 lime and zest. Cake had a very nice flavor and not to sweet.

Really good & moist! My first try at pound cake and it is a keeper. I didn't have lemon extract, but did have fresh lemon so I used same amount of juice, came out great! I have tried many recipes over the years and have learned to make 1/2 a recipe to see if good or not before I waste ingredients. so I made this in a mini Bundt pan and still baked it about 55 minutes. Will make a whole recipe next time!

I’ve been making theses cakes for a long time. I did alter it to use 5 eggs and 3 cups of sugar per our family recipe. Used Crisco butter for the shortening. But make sure the butter and sugar are mixed well! Also I don’t use the vanilla extract. Then I used powdered sugar and lemon juice for a glaze. Everyone loves this cake!!!
I had to add more of the soda I wish I choose 7up instead of lemon-line soda
Added a little lemon juice
